function: p. 6: D3QN GNN agent jointly learns aerial RIS deployment (horizontal moves) and passive beamforming (DFT-codebook subarray steering switches) to maximize the weighted sum rate.
system: p. 3-4, 10: TDD downlink MU-MISO, BS M=8 ULA, K=4 single-antenna users, UAV-mounted passive reflecting RIS N=64 elements with discrete phase shifts, 3 GHz, direct link blocked.
method: p. 7-10: Dueling double DQN (D3QN) with GNN over user and RIS nodes, reinforcement learning with WSR reward; initialization network (JDBNet+) trained with WSR loss on Rician-generated data.
data_channel: p. 10-11: custom simulator; BS-RIS and RIS-user LoS Rician channels (factor 10), path loss 30+22log10(d) dB; initialization network data from Rician model; no 3GPP, dataset or measurements.
test_conditions: p. 14: trained with K=4 users and RIS height 80 m, then deployed without retraining at K=6 users and at 100 m height ('Mismatched'), compared with retrained 'Matched' models.
baselines: p. 11: random RIS beamforming (non-learned); DDQN [30], MO-PPO [32], D3QN [34] (learned); own ablations BFNet and BFNet+ without RIS movement.
metrics: p. 11-14: weighted sum rate (bits/s/Hz) versus episodes, steps, user distribution, N and subarrays; number of parameters (Table III).
complexity: p. 14: Table III parameters: JDBNet 66,158, JDBNet+ 103,920, BFNet 57,448 versus DDQN 323,591, MO-PPO 182,470, D3QN 1,303,749; no FLOPs or runtime.
q1_support: p. 10: "These channels are modeled using a Rician fading channel with a Rician factor of 10." p. 11: "30 + 22 log10 (d) (dB)" is the path loss. Custom Rician simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 14: "directly deploying the network trained for K = 4 to a scenario with K = 6 achieves performance comparable to that of a network trained explicitly for K = 6"; the model trained at 80 m RIS height is also deployed at 100 m without retraining.
q3_support: p. 11: "We also include the DDQN proposed in [30], MO-PPO proposed in [32], and decaying double DQN (D3 QN) proposed in [34] as a benchmark" (learned); "Incorporating DRL to adjust the RIS beamforming yields significant performance gains compared to randomly setting the RIS beamforming" (non-learned); all compared on WSR (Fig. 5, Table III).
q4_support: p. 14: "The number of parameters and performance after training convergence are listed in Table III." Table III gives 66,158 (JDBNet) and 103,920 (JDBNet+) parameters versus 323,591 for DDQN; no FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 10: "When training the initialization network, we utilize the Rician channel model to generate the dataset." Synthetic Rician data; no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere (the only URL is the IEEE rights notice, p. 1).
notes: Included under area 3: the agent learns RIS passive beamforming jointly with the placement of the UAV-mounted RIS (p. 6, A = M x P_L), so the above_phy exclusion for UAV placement does not apply; the ZF active precoder is not learned (p. 5). Area 6 could be argued because the RIS is carried by a UAV, but the paper never mentions NTN, satellite or HAPS links and models a terrestrial 3 GHz LoS Rician link (p. 10); the reviewer may reassign.
